name: Classical Sanskrit Literature
description: One of the oldest literary traditions, encompassing the Vedas, epics (Mahabharata, Ramayana), and classical drama and poetry

name: Classical Greek Literature
description: Foundation of Western literary tradition, from Homeric epics through Athenian drama and philosophical dialogues

name: Classical Latin Literature
description: Roman literary tradition spanning the Republic and Empire, deeply influenced by Greek models while developing distinctive genres like satire

name: Classical Chinese Literature
description: One of the longest continuous literary traditions, from the Book of Songs through Tang poetry and the Four Great Classical Novels

name: Classical Arabic Literature
description: Rich tradition from pre-Islamic poetry through the golden age of Abbasid literature, deeply intertwined with Islamic civilization

name: Classical Japanese Literature
description: Distinguished by aesthetic refinement, from Man'yoshu poetry through The Tale of Genji and Noh drama

name: Old English Literature
description: Anglo-Saxon literary tradition combining Germanic heroic verse with Christian themes
sources: ["The Cambridge Companion to Old English Literature"]

name: Persian Classical Literature
description: Persian literary golden age producing some of the world's greatest epic and lyric poetry

name: Medieval European Literature
description: Vernacular literary traditions of medieval Europe including troubadour poetry, chivalric romance, and allegory
notable_authors: ["Chretien de Troyes","Dante Alighieri","Geoffrey Chaucer","Wolfram von Eschenbach"]
sources: ["The Cambridge History of Medieval English Literature"]

name: Classical Tamil Literature
description: Sangam literature and post-Sangam works forming one of the oldest classical literary traditions in India

name: Russian Literary Tradition
description: The golden and silver ages of Russian literature, producing psychologically profound novels and poetry

name: West African Oral Literature
description: Rich oral literary traditions including griot-transmitted epics, folktales, and praise poetry
